summary: Updates a rigid body's world position by adding a caller-supplied delta vector, then extracts two Euler angles from the body's orientation matrix with atan2 (with a dedicated branch for the gimbal-lock case where the pitch cosine magnitude is 1.0), and applies the transform through sub_56F100. Wraps the computation in an FPU control-word save/restore and routes the restore-mismatch path through an empty stub.

operations.description: Save the FPU control word precision mask with FPUControlWordMaskExtract, comparing against the constant 512.
Load the rigid body state pointer from this + 0x15F0.
Add the incoming delta vector components to the body's stored position (fields this + 0x15F4, +0x15FC, +0x1604).
Read the pitch-related component at this + 0x1634, negate it, and pass it through FloatConvertWrapper.
Detect the gimbal-lock case: the absolute value of the this + 0x1634 component equals the 1.0 constant global.
Gimbal-lock branch: first Euler angle from atan2 of the negated this + 0x163C component over this + 0x160C, with the second angle fixed to zero.
General branch: extract two Euler angles with atan2 of this + 0x161C over this + 0x164C and this + 0x1624 over this + 0x162C.
Apply the accumulated position and computed orientation to the rigid body via sub_56F100.
When the restored FPU control word no longer equals 512, divert through EmptyStub_7780 instead of returning the result.
Return sub_56F100's result on the matching-control-word path, otherwise the empty stub result.

unresolved: The exact meaning of the atan2 pairs (rotation matrix elements versus quaternion components) and the roles of the intermediate this + 0x15F4..+0x164C double fields are read from the raw arithmetic only.
Whether the delta vector a2 is a world-space velocity, offset, or acceleration is caller-defined and not visible here.
The 512 constant and the EmptyStub_7780 diversion on control-word mismatch are FPU-state hygiene whose game-specific intent is unknown.
